messages:
Maya: Quick architecture question — our policy decision graph currently does random tie-break selection when multiple routes score similarly. During surge tests that randomness causes a lot of route-churn and observable latency oscillation. Thinking about changing to a hybrid deterministic+probabilistic approach. Anyone seen this pattern before?

Raj: yeah saw that in the canary last week. results: cold-starts on some regions + random picks -> oscillation across shards. :grimacing:

Ava: inertia (stickiness window) helped in past, but it delayed failover when a node actually degraded. there’s a tradeoff between stability and responsiveness.

Maya: exactly. my rough idea: pick the highest-scoring route deterministically as primary. if score gap < epsilon, use a weighted-random fallback where weights are proportional to softmax(score/temperature). also add a short decay window for previously chosen primary to avoid hot-flipping. pseudocode: 
``` 
if (best_score - second_best_score) > EPSILON:
  choose(best)
else:
  probs = softmax([best, second_best], temp)
  choose_random(probs)
if last_pick_age < MIN_INERTIA && current_choice != last_choice:
  stick_with(last_choice)
``` 

Ben: I like that — gives us deterministic behaviour when clearly better, but still lets traffic probe alternatives when scores are noisy. need to define EPSILON and temperature per-tenant maybe.

Raj: agree per-tenant knobs. also we should surface a route-choice entropy metric so we can alert when randomness is driving too much churn.

infra-bot: FYI: route_churn spikes observed at 2025-11-17T16:12Z correlate with increased p99 by ~9%. traces: https://grafana.redwood/example/d/route-churn

Ava: for rollback safety, ensure tie-breaks are deterministic across controller restarts when seed is fixed. otherwise you get divergent decisions during a rollout. maybe seed with policy_id + epoch?

Maya: good point. seed deterministically for experiments, but allow true randomness for production with telemetry gating. also want to avoid global locking — decisions must be local and cheap.

Ben: for validation I'll add a sim harness: run 10k synthetic requests under surge with current random tie-break vs hybrid. command: `./sim/run --policy decision-graph.json --scenario surge-1000x --runs 200`

Raj: can we also run a quick A/B in staging where we enable the hybrid for a single tenant and measure latency & cost delta for 24h?

Maya: yes. plan: 1) add config knobs + deterministic seed option, 2) sim runs and telemetry addition (entropy, churn rate), 3) small staging A/B, 4) gradual roll with canary.

Ava: +1 — please add a short RFC doc or PR description listing defaults for EPSILON, temperature, and inertia window, and the metrics we'll collect.

Maya: will do. @Ben can you spin up the sim and drop results in this thread? I'll draft PR with config schema and tests. :thumbsup:
